stories.head: Constructor reports 900% growth in AI agent customers as agentic commerce accelerates
stories.plain: Constructor's 900% growth in AI agent customers signals that agentic commerce tools are moving from experiment to mainstream purchase. Nextview joining the Claude network also shows vendors betting on agent-to-agent interoperability. These adoption signals matter because they reshape which platforms buyers evaluate and how budgets shift.

stories.head: Experiential retail media emerges as a new in-store discovery channel
stories.plain: The piece argues that physical retail is the next retail media frontier, outperforming social and search for product discovery. For MarTech buyers, this means in-store data integration and personalization tooling become relevant spend categories, connecting CDP and CEP investments to brick-and-mortar touchpoints.

stories.head: Direct mail resurfaces as a precision ABM channel for technology marketers
stories.plain: Tech marketers are reviving direct mail not as broadcast but as a measured, account-based tactic tied to specific sales motions. This matters for MarTech planning because it signals budget and data flows moving back into offline channels, requiring CDP integrations and attribution tooling to track ROI rigorously.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams via Acquisition of DoubleO.ai
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and launched Agent Teams, a product that coordinates multiple AI agents across a company's data, signals, and systems to execute full go-to-market plays without human babysitting at each step. This matters because it signals that agentic GTM automation is moving from demos into shipping products backed by major martech acquirers.

stories.head: Salesforce Acquires AI Customer Research Startup Listen Labs
stories.plain: Salesforce bought Listen Labs, which runs AI-powered customer interviews and can simulate customer behavior. The acquisition pulls AI-driven customer insight directly into Salesforce's CRM and agent layer, shortening the loop between understanding buyers and acting on that understanding — relevant to anyone buying or building on the Salesforce stack.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Reshape Brand and Price Competition
stories.plain: New Jellyfish data shows AI shopping assistants build their own 'AI shelves' that don't mirror traditional brand rankings or price tiers. Jellyfish also launched a Share of Model™ Shopping Optimization product. This reframes how marketers must think about visibility inside AI-mediated purchase decisions, not just search rankings.

stories.head: Braze Expands AI from Content Creation to Full Campaign Operations
stories.plain: Braze added tools that automate campaign quality checks, give marketers easier access to AI decisioning, and connect the platform to external LLMs including Anthropic's Claude. This is a meaningful product shift — moving Braze from a messaging runner into a platform that can reason about when, how, and to whom messages go.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust™ to Add Continuous Intent Verification to Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem now includes DataDome, which continuously checks whether an AI agent's live actions match what it was originally authorized to do — not just verifying identity at login. This tackles a real governance gap in agentic commerce: agents that start legitimate can drift or be hijacked mid-transaction.

themes.head: AI Raised the Bar: Customers Expect More, Tolerate Less
body: AI has quietly reset the baseline for what a 'good' customer experience looks like. Because consumers now routinely interact with AI that is instant, personalised, and frictionless, any brand experience that falls short of that standard feels actively worse than it did two years ago — not just average.

This expectation gap is widening faster than most marketing teams are moving. The lesson from Mixbook's deliberate choice to hide its AI from customers is telling: the brand benefit comes from the outcome, not the label, and over-promising on AI while under-delivering on experience is now a trust liability.
ev: Agile Brand · Mixbook's silent AI strategy

themes.head: Agentic AI Enters the Stack — and Nobody's Watching It
body: The shift from AI as a tool to AI as an autonomous agent acting inside go-to-market workflows is accelerating. ZoomInfo's acquisition of DoubleO.ai to launch 'Agent Teams', DataDome joining Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem, and Growth7 turning CRM data into autonomous pipeline actions all signal that agents are no longer a pilot project — they are live infrastructure.

The governance problem is real and largely unsolved. MarTech's warning that GTM teams are losing track of their AI agents is the necessary counterweight: as agents multiply across the stack, the risk of compounding errors, rogue spend, and brand-inconsistent actions rises sharply, and most teams lack the audit layer to catch them.

themes.head: The AI Search Disruption Rewrites Visibility Rules
body: Generative engine results are reshaping which brands get found — and the old SEO playbook does not translate cleanly. Jellyfish research shows AI shopping recommendations are upending brand leadership and price positioning, while MarTech data busts seven widely-held myths about how AI search actually surfaces content, forcing marketers to rethink authority signals, visual assets, and structured data.

The practical response is a new content discipline: optimising for generative engine models rather than keyword rankings, building visual SEO strategies tuned to multimodal AI, and accepting that the click-through funnel brands relied on for a decade may no longer be the primary discovery path for high-intent buyers.
ev: MarTech Series · Jellyfish AI shopping research

themes.head: B2B Has an Evidence Gap, Not a Budget Gap
body: The persistent complaint that B2B marketing 'can't prove ROI' is being reframed as a measurement and data-quality problem, not a spend problem. The AI-shaped buyer journey — where research happens inside LLMs and dark social before any trackable click — is making attribution even harder, pushing CMOs to invest in buyer-intent intelligence rather than last-touch attribution.

Circle & Square's buyer intelligence guide and the Comcast research showing TV and streaming driving full-funnel results both point to the same fix: build a richer evidence base across the whole journey, including channels that resist direct attribution, rather than cutting spend on anything that lacks a clean conversion line.
ev: Agile Brand · CMO AI buyer journey guide
MarTech Series · Comcast full-funnel TV research

themes.head: Retail & Commerce Media Goes Physical and Agentic
body: Retail media is escaping the digital shelf. Experiential retail media is putting brand moments back in physical aisles, while AI-powered platforms like CommerceIQ are automating the entire bid-to-outcome loop on commerce marketplaces including Chewy. The channel is simultaneously going more physical and more algorithmically managed — a combination that demands new creative and data skills from brand teams.

The broader pattern — direct mail resurging for tech brands, CTV gaining verified-supply infrastructure via Jamloop, Particular Audience launching trade media — suggests a deliberate flight back to channels with verified reach and tangible proof of delivery, as AI-driven fraud and measurement noise erode confidence in purely digital, programmatic inventory.
ev: MarTech Series · CommerceIQ Chewy AI launch
Agile Brand · Direct mail still works for tech

month.takeaway: Across every theme this month, the same tension surfaces: AI is accelerating capability and expectation simultaneously, meaning the brands that win will be those that govern their AI infrastructure as rigorously as they deploy it.
